We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of $\mathrm{^{13}CO(J=1-0)}$ line and 104 GHz continuum emission from NGC 604, a giant H region (GHR) in the nearby spiral galaxy M33.
The target was observed with the ALMA 12m array on 18 January 2015 for a total of 60 minutes on-source.

ALMA was in configuration C34-2/1 with 34 antennas (although two are flagged as unusable) arranged with baselines ranging from 15 m to 349 m, which yields a minimum beam angular resolution of 2.2 arcsec and a maximum recoverable scale of 29 arcsec (at 110.27 GHz).

findings_qualitative.value: GMCs in NGC 604 are at different evolutionary stages, with clouds near the centre associated with continuum and active star formation (L1/MMS4, L4/MMS2, L5/MMS1) and outer clouds only detected in 13CO line emission.

evidence.quote: We have labelled the three continuum sources with the abbreviation MMS (millimetre source), with MMS1 corresponding to L5, MMS2 corresponding to L4, and MMS4 corresponding to L1 as seen in the bottom right panel of Figure 1.

We only detect 104 GHz continuum emission near the centre of GHR. Further out of the centre, only $^{13}$CO line emission is detected. This indicates that the GMCs in NGC 604 are in different evolutionary stages as previously suggested by (cite: Tosaki2007) and (cite: Miura2010).

claims.hypothesis: Whether the 13CO(J=1-0) molecular clouds in NGC 604 follow the Larson size-linewidth relation observed in the Milky Way and NGC 300.
claims.experiment: Measured cloud radii R and rms linewidths Delta v for 15 leaves and 4 branches using ASTRODENDRO and computed the Spearman correlation coefficient.
claims.result: Sizes and linewidths are correlated with Spearman r_s = 0.8, but the relation is offset below the Milky Way and NGC 300 relations at small radii.
claims.finding: The size-linewidth correlation supports compressible hierarchical turbulence, while the offset from Milky Way and NGC 300 relations is likely due to limited resolution or truncation bias from the dendrogram bijection approach on bright structures.

evidence.quote: The Spearman correlation coefficient for these data has the value of $\mathrm{r_{s}=0.8}$, which indicates that there is a correlation between size and linewidths of GMCs in NGC 604.
The relation for the NGC 604 clouds does not match the Milky Way and NGC 300 slopes; the linewidths at small radii for the NGC 604 data fall below the Milky Way and NGC 300 relations.

We have found that the sizes and linewidths are correlated for the NGC 604 GMCs but that the relationship is offset from the Milky Way scaling relation. This may be a consequence of the limited resolution of our data or artefact of the dendrogram analysis as applied to bright sources.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular clouds in NGC 604 are in approximate virial equilibrium.
claims.experiment: Derived virial masses M_vir and 13CO luminosity-based masses M_lum for the 15 identified clouds and calculated the virial parameter alpha_vir and Spearman correlation coefficient.
claims.result: M_vir and M_lum are strongly correlated with Spearman r_s = 0.98, and alpha_vir ranges from 0.2 to 1.1.
claims.finding: The molecular clouds in NGC 604 are in near virial equilibrium or in a state of forming stars.

evidence.quote: We show in Figure 6 that the clouds in NGC 604 are in near virial equilibrium and that the data are strongly correlated, with a Spearman coefficient of $r_{s}=0.98$.
These clouds have virial parameters ranging from 0.2-1.1, indicating that some clouds are in virial equilibrium while others could be in a state of forming stars.

claims.hypothesis: GMCs in NGC 604 are at different evolutionary stages with sequential star formation driven by the expanding giant HII region.
claims.experiment: Compared the spatial distributions of ALMA 13CO(J=1-0) line emission and 104 GHz free-free continuum emission across NGC 604.
claims.result: 104 GHz continuum emission is only detected near the centre of the GHR (associated with L1, L4, L5) and its peaks are spatially offset closer to the HII region centre than the 13CO peaks, while outer clouds only show 13CO emission.
claims.finding: GMCs in NGC 604 are in different evolutionary stages: central clouds associated with continuum are actively forming stars and photoionizing gas, while outer 13CO-only clouds are cold dense molecular clouds without active star formation.

evidence.quote: As seen in Figure 2, both continuum and $^{13}$CO(J=1-0) emission are detected near the centre of the H region, although at locations further from the centre of the H region, we found a few locations with only $^{13}$CO(J=1-0) emission.

We only detect 104 GHz continuum emission near the centre of GHR. Further out of the centre, only $^{13}$CO line emission is detected. This indicates that the GMCs in NGC 604 are in different evolutionary stages as previously suggested by (cite: Tosaki2007) and (cite: Miura2010).

why_this_data.value: Archival ALMA Band 3 observations of NGC 604 have better resolution and sensitivity compared to prior observations, helping to resolve individual GMCs and overcome low-sensitivity biases in extragalactic GMC studies.

evidence.quote: In this work, we present a dendrogram analysis of ALMA observations of $^{13}$CO(J=1-0) and 104 GHz continuum emission from NGC 604. These observations have better resolutions and sensitivities compared to prior observations, which helps to overcome many of the issues highlighted by (cite: Faesi2018).

why_this_method.value: ASTRODENDRO decomposes emission into a hierarchy of nested structures, providing a precise representation of the topology of star-forming complexes; Briggs robust = 0.5 was chosen to improve angular resolution without severely compromising sensitivity.

evidence.quote: We used Briggs weighting with the robust parameter set to 0.5 to improve the angular resolution of the final images without severely compromising the image sensitivity.

To identify structures within the $^{13}$CO(J=1-0) image cube, we used the ASTRODENDRO package, which decomposes emission into a hierarchy of nested structures (cite: Rosolowsky2008; Colombo2015). This dendrogram technique, provide a precise representation of the topology of star forming complexes.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Lowering the ASTRODENDRO detection threshold from 4 sigma_rms to 3 sigma_rms to detect fainter NMA clouds (NMA 1, 3, 6, 11, 12) was rejected because it introduced spurious noise detections.

evidence.quote: If we lower our detection threshold to 3$\sigma$, we can detect these sources, but we also detect additional spurious noise in the maps. Given this situation, we chose to use only sources detected at the higher threshold.

limitations_admitted.value: Scatter of 0.3 dex in the X_13CO conversion factor causes a systematic uncertainty of about a factor of 2 in the derived luminous masses.

evidence.quote: The scatter in $\mathrm{X_{^{13}CO}}$ value is 0.3 dex (cite: Cormier2018). This uncertainty means that masses will have a systematic error of about a factor of 2.

limitations_admitted.value: The bijection approach in dendrogram analysis underestimates rms linewidths (and thus virial masses) for leaves defined by high isocontour levels because the spectral line wings are truncated by the isosurface boundary.

evidence.quote: The rms linewidths in the dendrogram analysis tend to be underestimated for structures which are defined by high isocontour levels such as leaves because the full width of the spectral line is truncated by the isosurface boundary (cite: Rosolowsky2005; Rosolowsky2008).

Most of the clouds are lying below a one-to-one relation, illustrating that the masses estimated from the luminosities are slightly higher than the virial masses, which is a direct consequence of underestimating linewidths as discussed in the previous section.

limitations_admitted.value: Limited spatial resolution prevents separating L5 into smaller constituent clouds and may contribute to the offset in the size-linewidth relation.

evidence.quote: It is possible that L5 contains two or more smaller clouds, but we could not separate them into smaller clouds when applying ASTRODENDRO to the $^{13}$CO data.
This may be a consequence of the limited resolution of our data or artefact of the dendrogram analysis as applied to bright sources.

limitations_admitted.value: 13CO(J=1-0) only traces dense gas and resolves away diffuse gas that makes up larger-scale structures.

evidence.quote: This is attributed to $^{13}$CO(J=1-0) only tracing the dense gas, hence, resolving away diffuse gas which make up large scale structure and also to the underestimation of linewidths.

referee_caveats_inferred: Table 1 (referenced as Table [tab:Cloud Properties]) is missing from the text, preventing verification of individual cloud measurements.

The continuum frequency is referred to as 104 GHz throughout the text, whereas Section 2 states the fourth spectral window covered continuum from 98.56 to 99.50 GHz; it is not stated whether all line-free channels across all four spectral windows (spanning ~96.7 to 110.2 GHz, average ~104 GHz) were combined to make the continuum image.

It is not explicitly stated whether the measured spatial sizes (sigma_maj, sigma_min) and velocity dispersion (Delta v) were deconvolved by the synthesized beam and channel width before computing R and M_vir.
No correction for short-spacing / missing flux is applied (12m array only), although the maximum recoverable scale (116 pc) is larger than the identified cloud sizes (5-21 pc).

reproducibility.score_reason: Raw ALMA data are public (2013.1.00639.S), CASA version (5.6.1), imaging pixel scale (0.36 arcsec), channel width (0.664 km/s), Briggs robust (0.5), achieved rms, and ASTRODENDRO thresholds (4 sigma min_value, 3 sigma min_delta) and mass conversion formulas are explicitly stated. However, tclean cleaning thresholds/masks, ASTRODENDRO min_npix, beam deconvolution choices, and the table of individual cloud properties are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public archival dataset with standard pipeline calibration, straightforward tclean imaging, and an open-source ASTRODENDRO analysis workflow yielding clear numeric benchmarks (number of leaves/branches, mass and size ranges, Spearman correlations, NMA-8 and NMA-9 masses).

methods_papers.why: Dendrogram structure decomposition algorithm, bijection approach, luminous mass formula, and bootstrap error estimation
Hierarchical dendrogram decomposition of molecular gas structures
Approach for extracting molecular cloud physical properties from ASTRODENDRO
Spherical radius definition (R = 1.91 sigma_r) and bootstrap uncertainty method
Spherical radius definition, virial mass formulation, and Milky Way scaling relation

companion_papers.why: Analyzed the same region/ALMA millimeter continuum sources (MMS1, MMS2, MMS3) in NGC 604
Earlier NMA 12CO(1-0) study of NGC 604 providing the NMA cloud catalog compared throughout the paper
